"I feel like this is exactly why women don’t come forward. If you’re not a perfect victim with a perfect story, you’re lying or you’re crazy.” #MeToo 
(I feel this in the marrow of my bones)

As a victim who has been personally harmed by the NYPD Special Victims Unit I want to remind everyone that this is a systemic problem, change does not happen overnight, and actions speak louder than words and press pieces. 
#MeToo  
https://t.co/3oJoKzYsJ5

The NYPD tells victims of sex crimes that they want us to report, that they’re ready with resources to bring us justice. But I know from first hand experience after reporting in 2017, the NYPD did not show me victim centric care, they showed me callous disregard. #MeToo
After time it became clear to me that the NYPD wasn’t interested in getting justice for me or for any other survivor, and that nothing was going to change unless I changed it myself. #MeToo

I had to become my own advocate, following up & speaking out. I had to demand to be heard by the higher-ups at the NYPD. I had to speak to the press to get my case taken seriously. I had to be my own support system & fight every day just to be heard by anyone at the NYPD. #MeToo

And I’m not alone.  It should never be on the back of victims to have to fight to be believed and supported within a system designed for victims of sexual violence, and certainly not one that the NYPD touts is “victim centric.” #MeToo

Our job is not to hold the NYPD accountable; our job is to heal. That was stolen from me by the NYPD. Even now, more than 22 months after my assault, I’m still unable to start the job of healing, simply because the NYPD hasn’t done theirs. #MeToo

I did what I was supposed to do: I reported, I have shown up every time the NYPD asked me to - whenever they’ve asked me to be somewhere, I’ve been there, on the phone, in person I have been available to them day and night, no matter how difficult the request. #MeToo

I have been willing to relive my trauma, to share my pain, to do whatever it takes to help the NYPD help me. And all the while, they couldn’t even be bothered to answer a simple email. They have ignored me, belittled me, dismissed me. #MeToo

The NYPD has made a mockery of me, of my case, and of the city I love. I deserve better. Survivors deserve better. New Yorkers deserve better. And I will not stop fighting until we get what we deserve. #MeToo

The fall is always a hard time for me. October is the anniversary of my most recent assault, Kavanaugh confirmation, & the resurgence of the #MeToo movement. 
Thank you @DanaSussman for sending me this (and telling me I’m featured 49sec into it). It reminds me how strong we are!

Notice the one thing missing from this @NBCNewYork piece is a victim who has reported to NYPD SVD sharing their experience. You never hear directly from a victim. 
#MeToo
https://t.co/0Av69WkGBR
I have worked hard to hold the NYPD accountable and push them to be victim centric: https://t.co/VNlMUT2GXC #MeToo

Again, it should never be on the back of victims to have to fight to be believed. #MeToo
https://t.co/ZE3yuQtKvD

NYPD says they’re taking a more “victim centric approach” but their actions prove otherwise. They did NOT believe @annaaachambers and they’re doing everything wrong by her. @annaaachambers deserves justice! #MeToo  
https://t.co/aInUmlJzCx…

Chanel Miller is amazing.
#MeToo

Men are terrified that they’ll be replaced, but even *MORE* terrified that they’ll be replaced by the women whose power they attempted to take away, who they worked to silence for so long. 
To me it’s not replacement. It’s taking power back and it’s beautiful to witness. 
#MeToo

My first sexual experience was rape. I was 16. My second sexual experience was rape. I was 18. It took me years to realize and put a name to it.
My entire life I've struggled with boundaries, healthy relationships, trust issues, PTSD, and more. 
#MeToo
Once again we see that the life of a rapist is more important than the people he harmed. #MeToo

As the “rider” in this statement from @lyft I’d like to affirm what @rachsyme said. 
#metoo
I deserve better. Survivors deserve better. New Yorkers deserve better. And I will not stop fighting until we get what we deserve. #MeToo

I filed my own IAB complaint against my first NYPD SVD detective. She's still working and the results of the investigation were that my "case was too complex for her". We need to hold the NYPD SVD accountable. We need to hold the system accountable.
#MeToo

This is *NOT* the story of a man who lost his career. This *IS* the story of incredible women who have come forward, who are reclaiming their power, who we all should be inspired by. I want them centered in this story. I want to lift them up. I am grateful for them. #MeToo

I talked with @AmandaMarcotte at @Salon about why I’m working to hold @lyft accountable. 
#MeToo https://t.co/PojG38vYNi

I spoke with @TheFoldMag about what healing looks like for me, why I'm sharing my story and working to hold @lyft and the NYPD accountable, how much my friends mean to me, and how you can show up and support victims.
#MeToo 
https://t.co/H0zBdLGaf4

The last few paragraphs of my interview with @TheFoldMag are something I especially want to highlight. Showing up and supporting victims in your life is vital. 
#MeToo https://t.co/gKYbjIEkSb

How did you show up for a survivor in your life today? 
#MeToo https://t.co/c71pmDoRtL

Investigators are taught to only offer condolences to alleged victims that distance @Uber from a purported incident: “No one should have to go through something like that” rather than “I am so sorry that happened to you.”
#MeToo

I didn’t realize until today, when I met with @SenBlumenthal’s office, that my lawsuit against @lyft catalyzed this letter. This is why I share my story — survivors deserve true champions in Congress, corporations, and the criminal justice system. #MeToo
https://t.co/gHym5v4VU6

As we head into the 3yr anniversary of the "grab 'em by the pussy" tape, the 2yr anniversary of the Harvey Weinstein story breaking, and the 1yr anniversary of Dr. Blasey Ford testifying I'm sure there will be a million think pieces, panels, etc... please remember this #MeToo 1/

Include victims + survivors in everything. Center us in your stories, ensure we're on your panels, reach out to us to WRITE the story, to moderate the panel! Don't erase our trauma, don't pretend we don't exist. Don't say we're hard to find, that's a bullshit excuse. #MeToo  2/

If you're looking for survivors in your area to include on a panel, LMK and I'll help you. If you're writing a story and are looking for survivor voices, LMK and I'll help you. Don't be lazy and say "we tried to find survivors but couldn't". Again, that's bullshit. #MeToo 3/

This can be an incredibly hard time of year for many of us, for sure. But that doesn't mean we can't speak for ourselves about our own experiences. Center us, live your values, don't just talk the talk. I am here raising my hand and offering to be a resource for you. #MeToo 4/
Thank you for coming to my TedTalk, which will never end because I will never stop working to lift up and center survivor and victim stories. We are our best champions. #MeToo 5/5

I second this motion. 
#MeToo

A real sentence I just said to a journalist: "I don't know, I'm not a trauma expert. I've just experienced a lot of it in my life".
#MeToo

How a button became one of the greatest #MeToo victories via @voxdotcom

I sat down with @AndrewJenks and shared my story for this episode. You'll hear more about the days after I reported, about the neglect from the NYPD, and from experts who will help you understand why there's no "perfect victim narrative". #MeToo 
https://t.co/jTf6g1MDX5

This is happening while some victims are barely able to leave their house because of depression, PTSD, and fear of safety because they came forward. These men are making money while victims can barely, if at all, afford therapy. I'm so fucking sick of it.
#MeToo

Imagine a world where @lyft put the time, energy + budget to make this monthly membership into living their supposed value of “the safety of our passengers is our #1 priority”. 
I don’t want to see words from Lyft leadership I want to see ACTIONS! #MeToo

Dr. Blasey Ford inspires us all. #MeToo

I always say “the truth is not flexible”, and I believe as survivors we know that. However, it’s often people in our own lives, and the system, who deem us not credible. 
#MeToo #BelieveSurvivors

Riders, victims and survivors should never be limited in the ways we are able to hold these companies accountable. When harm is perpetrated against us control is taken away, and that’s what companies like @lyft are continuing to do when they amend their terms of service. #MeToo

I took a photo of a cop holding my rape kit, in 2017, the day I reported. I did this because I was prepared to not be believed. Because I assumed the NYPD would lose the kit, or it would sit on a shelf or in a warehouse for years. 
Victims deserve better. #MeToo

As a rape survivor I have a hard time with relationships, specifically romantic. My therapist gave me homework before our session next week. Sharing because others may appreciate these questions. 
#MeToo https://t.co/hzGovTNgSa

I don't want to be quick to praise @Uber and @lyft for releasing these reports. We pressured them, survivors did this work. They didn't do this on their own. It's on the backs of those who have been harmed, we fought for this. You're welcome! #MeToo

Don't forget that @uber made the pledge to release this report in 2017, after @CNN reported 103 drivers were accused of sexual assault or abuse. It was survivors sharing their stories, filing lawsuits, holding these companies accountable that finally got them to do this. #MeToo

Survivors and victims shifted the narrative around safety on ride share platforms. It was then that companies followed suit. Where are survivors in this conversation? Where are we in the decision making process? Right now we are nothing but data points, and percentages. #MeToo

Imagine if @uber used this money to actually live their supposed values? To actually make safety their #1 priority? When I was being kidnapped at gunpoint, taken across state lines, and gang raped by my driver and 2 others...no...this wouldn't have helped at all. 
#MeToo

This makes me ill. There’s no personal accountability here. And the fact that victims have to work alongside creditors to seek justice is horrifying. I never want to hear another person say “#MeToo has gone too far” or “lives of these men have been ruined” 🙄

A date is the fucking least of my worries, Donna. I’m stepping into my power. Holding systems, not just individuals, but SYSTEMS accountable. I regret nothing. We are opening our own doors, the doors to justice. Opening doors for ourselves and society. You’re welcome. 🙏🏻 #MeToo
